paragraphs: Ad Astra sells scheduling and academic planning software to colleges and universities. One platform covers course scheduling and campus event management for higher education institutions.

Schedulers build sections on a visual grid, handling buildings, spaces, faculty and room assignments in the same workflow. Recommendations drawn from historical enrollment patterns point to changes that ease course bottlenecks. Finished schedules and later edits publish straight to the campus student information system. Event requests and approvals run through workflows the institution sets up. Public event calendars can be viewed by category and embedded on a campus website.

The company says it partners with more than 550 institutions. Its analytics carry a measure it calls Degree Velocity, built on patented technology meant to improve student progress. Onboarding covers implementation, data imports and customized training rather than setup alone. Ad Astra also states a commitment to digital accessibility.

quote.text: Higher education’s first platform to integrate course planning and scheduling software for addressing student needs while promoting financial sustainability.
